thread:
maya: Heads up — sharing the PRD draft for the routing + failover contracts. Need signoff on acceptance criteria and edge cases before planning work in the sprint. Pls read and call out anything missing.

alex: skimmed — looks good overall. two macro q's: how strict are we about model-compatibility? i.e., do we allow fallback to a smaller-arch variant if exact weights not available?

maya: good Q. proposal in doc: tiered compatibility. primary: exact model id + quantization. secondary: same architecture + compatible tokenizer. tertiary: functionally equivalent smaller model only for latency-sensitive tiers. we should make this opt-in per customer.

samir: want explicit failure-mode behaviour. if fallback target exists but returns different shape/logits, what do we do? retry? translate? return degraded response?

lina: add acceptance criteria: (1) fallback decision deterministic and explainable in logs, (2) end-to-end latency stays within SLO for the tier, (3) quality regression measured vs baseline prompt set not to exceed X% on BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim.

maya: yes to all. draft acceptance checklist in PRD: 
- Deployment: canary with 1% traffic in region A, 5% in region B
- Observability: per-request route chain + policy id 
- Telemetry: fallback_count, fallback_reason, model_switched, latency_delta_ms 
- Quality guardrails: automated evals run on canary dataset, block rollout if >5% regression on critical prompts

alex: minor nit: telemetry keys should be snake_case to match existing conventions. also include "fallback_chain" array for postmortem.

maya: updated in doc. also added policy TTL: when a fallback decision is cached how long do we keep it? default 30s, configurable per route. thoughts?

samir: 30s seems fine as default. for long-lived sessions (chat), we need sticky routing for the conversation to avoid model hopping. add sticky_session: boolean at route level.

lina: edge case: cross-region latency spike — policy should prefer capacity fallback before crossing region if SLO risk. add acceptance test simulating region egress failure.

maya: called out. also adding rollout criteria: pass canary, run regression evals, run chaos test that kills one AZ and verify >=95% success rate for high-tier routes.

alex: can we define tiers clearly? propose: "latency-critical" (p95 < 200ms), "balanced" (p95 < 800ms), "cost-optimized" (best-effort). each tier has allowed fallback classes and max quality delta.

maya: yes. wrote those exact numbers in PRD. we should map default model variants per tier. e.g., latency-critical -> quantized variant vQ1, balanced -> fp16, cost-optimized -> int8-agg.

samir: acceptance criteria for routing correctness: end-to-end test harness that replays production traffic for 24h on staging with injected capacity constraints and validates no customer requests exceed outage SLA. add ticket to infra for replay infra.

lina: added an "invariant" check: if a fallback increases token-generation cost by >2x, block unless explicitly allowed by route owner. helps avoid accidental cost explosions.

maya: good catch. also adding owner escalation path in doc: if fallback_count spikes >threshold, auto-open pager to oncall and notify route owner channel.

deploy-bot: build 7182: canary policy engine image pushed to staging. tests: unit 312 passed, integration 48/50 passed.

alex: for RFC/PRD finalization: i'll draft a compact spec for the runtime team listing required control hooks (policy api, decision function, cache keys, signals). assign to me for eng-runtime work.

maya: thanks — i'll merge edits tonight. next steps: alex writes runtime spec, samir files replay infra ticket, lina drafts test matrix and quality thresholds. target: finalize PRD and get signoff by EOW. :thumbsup:

samir: filing replay ticket now, linking test harness doc.

lina: will create the quality prompt set and threshold doc, pinging research for help.

maya: awesome. small follow-up: include one example policy JSON in the PRD for clarity. here's a sketch to include:
```
{
  "policy_id": "tiered-failover-v1",
  "tiers": ["latency-critical","balanced","cost-optimized"],
  "compatibility": {
    "primary": ["model_id","quantization"],
    "secondary": ["architecture","tokenizer"],
    "tertiary": ["smaller_arch_variant"]
  },
  "sticky_session": true,
  "cache_ttl_seconds": 30
}
```

alex: perfect. that'll help eng-runtime implement quickly.

maya: cool. thanks all. i'll update thread when PRD is merged.

lina: :rocket:
